The article reports outcomes related to cancer pain control, including CR, PR, NC, and total response rate after treatment. I checked the results and tables for hemoglobinemia or any adverse-event outcome corresponding to hemoglobinemia grade ≥1, but no such outcome is reported. The only safety-related note is that one patient had severe liver dysfunction and was excluded from analysis, which does not match the requested hemoglobinemia definition. Although the randomized groups were 11 vs 11 and evaluable pain-analysis groups were 10 vs 10, these are not sample sizes for a matched hemoglobinemia outcome. Therefore, no extractable hemoglobinemia event counts are available.
